clue.text: Competition is a game of golf with hero's sidekick

parts.note: a round is one complete game over the course
Robin is Batman's sidekick in the comics

explanation.surface: A golf outing with a superhero's young partner is billed as a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a tournament format in which every entrant plays every other entrant.

clue.text: Beginning to object over unfriendly atmosphere

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next one
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of object is used

parts.note: the word object supplies just its opening letter
dour means stern and unfriendly

explanation.surface: Someone opens by objecting to a frosty mood in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell or, figuratively, a lingering aura or atmosphere around something.

clue.text: Man am I biased exhibiting an African country

indicators.note: exhibiting means putting on show, so the answer is displayed within the run of letters

parts.note: the words read as one string, with the country sitting across man, am, I and biased

explanation.surface: A man worries he shows prejudice in favour of an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa, bordering South Africa and Angola.

clue.text: Fled from Middle Eastern land with no leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone escaped from a Middle Eastern country that had lost its ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran is the past tense of run, meaning escaped or fled quickly.

clue.text: Military bigshots reportedly prohibited a music group

parts.note: top brass, or simply brass, is slang for high-ranking officers

indicators.note: reportedly signals that we go by what is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: Senior officers have, it is said, outlawed a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band is an ensemble of trumpets, cornets, tubas and similar instruments.

clue.text: Heard no noise from a horse

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Someone listens but catches nothing from a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the high whinnying call a horse makes.

clue.text: Duke, say, scoffing an Indian cheese

indicators.note: scoffing means eating greedily, so the peer takes the next letters inside

parts.note: a duke is an example of a peer, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A nobleman greedily wolfing down a portion of curd from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Paneer is a fresh, unaged curd made in South Asia and used in curries such as saag paneer.

clue.text: Standard article from northern France

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase matching the adjective Norman

parts.note: a norm is a standard or usual level
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A typical item originates in the north of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman describes Normandy, the region on the north coast of France.

clue.text: Some moan I'm a lawless beast

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, the letters sitting across them

parts.note: run together these words hold the beast across moan, I'm, a and lawless

explanation.surface: A moaner confesses to being an unruly brute.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal and beast are synonyms for a living creature, especially a non-human one.

clue.text: Crustacean runs inside taxi

indicators.note: inside places the runs abbreviation within the word for a taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A shellfish scuttles about within a cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is a ten-legged shelled sea creature, a classic crustacean.

clue.text: Almost yearn for leader's shenanigans

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to miss someone is to yearn for them
a chief is a leader

explanation.surface: Someone longs for their boss's playful tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief and shenanigans both mean playful misbehaviour or trickery.

clue.text: Creature in puma's lair disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of these words are the fodder to rearrange

explanation.surface: An animal is found in a big cat's den, which has been upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial, such as a kangaroo, is a mammal that carries its young in a pouch, so it is one kind of creature.

clue.text: Erica messily eats large dessert

indicators.note: eats means taking something inside, so the jumbled name surrounds the size abbreviation
messily suggests the name's letters are jumbled up

parts.note: the woman's name provides the five letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman called Erica untidily devours a big pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Duck down, right into a piece of furniture

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation for right goes inside the item of furniture

parts.note: a couch is a sofa, a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone ducks down and dives straight onto a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: To crouch is to bend the knees and lower the body, like ducking down.

clue.text: Reddish-brown and gold stream

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a small stream

explanation.surface: A brook shines in rusty and golden hues.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a Scottish word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a hair colour term for a red-brown shade.

clue.text: 90s music piece including Queen and old man

indicators.note: including means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a bit is a piece
R, from Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen
pop is a familiar word for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: A song featuring Queen and a father figure from the nineties.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band, but supplies the royal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was the guitar-based British pop style of the mid-1990s, with bands like Oasis and Blur.

clue.text: Dog located outside animal hospital

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: found means located
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A hound is discovered beyond the gates of a veterinary clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A foxhound is a breed of hunting dog trained to chase foxes.

clue.text: Carry bench, finally producing exasperated noise

parts.note: to hump is to carry something heavy with effort

indicators.note: finally picks out only the closing letter of the word bench

parts.note: the word bench supplies only its closing letter

explanation.surface: Lugging a heavy seat makes someone grunt in irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Humph is an interjection expressing doubt, annoyance or displeasure.

clue.text: I'm a leader of Muslims

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Muslims is used

parts.note: the word Muslims supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A religious figure introduces themselves as heading a Muslim congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Make amends around lunchtime, perhaps?

parts.note: at, as in at a time, gives a rough time
one o'clock is a typical lunchtime, hence the perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone plans to apologise over their midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is defined by example: one o'clock, and 'at one' is a natural phrase for that time.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make up for a wrong, that is, to make reparation.

clue.text: Naughty child initially ignores seafood

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of ignores is taken

parts.note: the word ignores supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky kid turns their nose up at the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, usually breaded and fried, a popular British seafood dish.

clue.text: Hint to head of espionage — move stealthily

parts.note: a tip is a hint or piece of advice
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of espionage is used

parts.note: the word espionage supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A spy chief is given advice on sneaking around.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to walk quietly on the balls of the feet to avoid being heard.

clue.text: Quirk of brief noise made by a clock

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a clock goes tick

explanation.surface: An odd habit consists of a short ticking from the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is a habitual twitch or idiosyncrasy, a personal quirk.

clue.text: Cheer pilot flying this?

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are tossed about into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words are the fodder to rearrange

explanation.surface: Would a cheerful aviator be at the controls of this aircraft?
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is a rotor-driven aircraft that a pilot might be flying.
